active_kv.label: SSD backing
active_kv.scope: Active decode KV only; prefill working KV remains in HBM. Retained-prefix placement is independent.
active_kv.model: Serialized tiled staging: remote reads + HBM-reference GPU service + append writes. No overlap or calibrated streaming-kernel correction.
active_kv.calibration: Unvalidated active-offload composition. GPU fits cover HBM-resident kernels; storage and transfer service use configured assumptions, not timings from the published request traces.
limitations: Fixed per-request residency fractions are assigned atomically at microbatch admission and remain pinned until completion; no dynamic promotion.

Initialization reserves decode GPU staging buffers and, when disaggregated, holds the handoff channel until backing is ready. Wire and device phases aggregate serial tile cycles; intermediate wire-end does not imply full-context GPU residency.
Remote payload is striped uniformly across tokens/layers. Aggregate transfer intervals represent serial chunked staging, not simultaneous full-context GPU residency.
GPU resources are held during remote I/O stalls; stage durations include those stalls once. Reference GPU operator times retain HBM memory access costs.
GPU energy charges activity only for reference GPU service, and idle power during I/O stalls. CPU/SSD/NIC and DMA power are excluded.
Initial prefill and retained-prefix restoration still require full prefill active KV in HBM. This model does not offload the prefill working set.

storage.batching_policy: Fixed uniform microbatches use the minimum restored prefix of their members; excess restored tokens are recomputed.

layout.label: SSD only
layout.description: Retain prefixes on SSD; charge SSD service and host–GPU transfers.

storage.policy: Retain prefixes on SSD; charge SSD service and host–GPU transfers. Cold start; blocking publication. Only completed contiguous prefixes are reusable; last prompt token is recomputed for logits.
limitations: Published request traces provide arrivals, token lengths and prefix identities, not measured SSD, DRAM, GDS or host-GPU service time. All storage and transfer timing uses configured assumptions with no measured error bound.
Dynamo-style policy is an approximation: independent LRU copies and a non-decaying request-reference disk filter, without Dynamo LFU aging, priorities or NIXL kernels.
GDS timing is configured startup + max(storage service, direct-link service); no measured GDS accuracy claim. No host relay or additional host-GPU copy is charged for direct GPU-SSD transfers.

Background publication retains its prefill source until publication and handoff both complete. Placement commits are serialized; background copies can overlap GPU computation and independent restores.
One replica per pool; fixed uniform batches, no continuous/ragged batching. Host and SSD capacities cover aggregate prefilling shard payloads.
HBM retained copies and active KV are separate allocations. One shared SSD bandwidth reservation prevents concurrent jobs multiplying bandwidth; no packet, NAND or detailed PCIe contention model.
GPU energy excludes SSD, CPU and transfer-device energy. Hit-fit validation is against trace-policy replay, not hardware cache telemetry.

protocol.candidates: F0–F8; embedding additionally F9 with fixed 16-token switch.
protocol.cohort_policy: BF16 KAIST and FP16 Vidur kept separate. No per-GPU/model coefficient selection.
protocol.grouping: Canonical executed operator geometry across GPU/model/TP; embedding groups token count and hidden width.
protocol.interpretation: Exploratory nested cross-validation within imported dense profile conditions, not a new-GPU or end-to-end serving error guarantee.
protocol.selection: Family and transition scale selected on inner folds only. Outer fold never fits or selects coefficients.

dataset.model: Nested-CV selected shape-informed functions; separate KAIST BF16 / Vidur FP16 fits; no runtime timing-table lookup

warnings: Behavioral simulation, not mechanistic simulation. Estimates do not model GPU instructions, cycles, page-level memory events or physical network packets; not measured hardware performance or a KAIST validation claim.
Fixed prefill microbatches with optional decode splitting; no cross-prefill merge or continuous rebatching. Independent FIFO phase admission limits are per replica and held across all chunks/tokens.

Uniform decoder layers with RMSNorm, RoPE and SwiGLU; optional QK normalization and routed experts. MLA, hybrid attention, shared experts, encoder-decoder and vision encoders are outside this architecture model.
Ideal KV SRAM read reuse; KV writes still reach HBM. HBM stores the complete KV payload.
Tensor tiling, uniform MoE routing, engine efficiency, activation traffic and activity-based energy are explicit assumptions. Quantization conversion overhead and numerical quality are excluded.
Pipeline activation messages use the limiting fabric tier of the entire pool as a conservative placement approximation.
Network tiers use the limiting end-to-end bandwidth plus ring/dispatch overhead; they do not model individual packets or switches.
TTFT includes batch formation, queueing, prefill and KV handoff; the first token is released after the handoff.

GPU operator service times use nested-CV selected shape-informed functions fitted to KAIST BF16 or Vidur FP16 profiles; no runtime timing-table lookup, GPU-ID correction or exact-match override. Profiled configurations also have prediction error.
Serving queues, network collectives, memory/traffic accounting and GPU energy remain behavioral estimates. Empirical residual percentiles on withheld data are not confidence bounds for every new GPU.

Training includes compatible dense profiles across five GPU families and two precision/software cohorts. Precision selects the historical calibration cohort; software-version changes remain unvalidated. Fused MoE, MLA, hybrid layers, cross-vendor hardware, quantization, clocks and architectural cache changes require additional validation. Unsupported operators retain analytical fallbacks.

Prefix retention: fixed uniform microbatches use a common restored-prefix floor, the selected retained-cache layout, configured asynchronous or blocking publication, and pinned prefill HBM allocations. Cache reuse skips query work while retaining full attention context.

Published request traces supply workload and prefix identities, not device-service timings. Storage and transfers use configured assumptions with no measured error bound. Trace-policy hit forecasts do not decide runtime hits. GPU energy excludes storage and host power.
GDS is a configured direct-path approximation, not measured GDS or Dynamo performance. Dynamo-style cache policy is simplified and does not reproduce its full scheduler.
Serialized tiled staging: remote reads + HBM-reference GPU service + append writes. No overlap or calibrated streaming-kernel correction.
Unvalidated active-offload composition. GPU fits cover HBM-resident kernels; storage and transfer service use configured assumptions, not timings from the published request traces.
Prefill active KV remains in HBM. Active decode backing and retained prefixes have independent placement and capacity accounting; they share SSD and host/GPU queues.

provenance.timing_source: GPU service functions fitted to KAIST/Vidur profiles; no GPU-ID selection; SimPy serving and analytical network
provenance.precision_note: Peak TFLOPS must use dense/non-sparse values. Weight precision changes bytes; KV precision is configured separately; conversion overhead is excluded. GB/TB are decimal.
